I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I farm on the North China Plain, so this is the cropping system I trust most for stable grain, familiar field work, and easier use of local machinery and irrigation. I will not spread myself across many crops, because at my age I want a system I know well and can manage on time. For wheat, I will stay with an improved variety, put most of the phosphorus in as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate at the key water stages, and keep sprays limited to the main disease, weed, and aphid pressure periods. After wheat harvest, I will direct-seed hybrid summer maize into the same land, keep fertilizer balanced but not excessive, irrigate only at the most important stages if water is short, and do pest control only when pressure is clear. My aim is steady yield with lower risk, not chasing the highest possible output.
